title: Acute Urinary Retention: Immediate Management and Urology Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with acute urinary retention (AUR) in the emergency department (ED) or primary care: recognition, bedside bladder ultrasound, urethral or suprapubic catheterisation, search for precipitants, post-obstructive diuresis, alpha blocker before a trial without catheter (TWOC), admission criteria and urology follow-up. Uses an ED clinical summary from South Eastern Sydney Local Health District (SESLHD), a peer-reviewed review of AUR in benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), and the alfuzosin label. Children and retention after recent urological surgery are excluded except for when to call urology.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-21.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi or national AUR guideline was found; NICE CG97 could not be opened.
The main sources are an ED clinical summary (derived from a textbook) and a 2007 review, which are lower than guideline tier.
The ED summary names oxybutynin 2.5 mg twice daily for catheter-related bladder spasm, but no label was opened, so it is not listed.
Tamsulosin is used for TWOC in practice but its AUR dose and label were not opened in this task, so only alfuzosin is listed.
Typical adult normal values for residual volume, creatinine and potassium are not from these sources.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: AUR is a sudden painful inability to pass urine with abdominal distension or pain, mostly in older men (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Definition). BPH causes bladder outlet obstruction and is the cause in at least 65% of men with AUR (AUR review 2007, Section Epidemiology). Causes fall into increased outflow resistance, loss of bladder innervation, and bladder over-distension (AUR review 2007, Section Etiopathogenesis). Anticholinergic drugs reduce detrusor contraction and alpha-agonists raise outlet resistance (AUR review 2007, Section Medications and AUR). Alpha blockers relax smooth muscle in the prostate, capsule and bladder neck, the dynamic part of the obstruction (AUR review 2007, Section Role of alpha blockers).

symptoms: Sudden inability to pass urine with lower abdominal pain (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Definition).
Previous lower urinary tract symptoms: urgency, frequency, hesitancy, weak stream, terminal dribbling, nocturia (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Clinical features).
Visible haematuria suggesting infection, stone or tumour (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Clinical features).
Back pain, leg weakness or numbness suggesting spinal cord compression (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Clinical features).
physicalSigns: Tender, distended bladder in the lower abdomen (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Clinical features).
Phimosis, paraphimosis, meatal stenosis or trauma on genital examination (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Clinical features).
Rectal examination: prostate size, anal tone and perineal sensation (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Clinical features).
Raised blood pressure or tachycardia, often transient (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Clinical features).
redFlags: Neurological deficit, reduced anal tone or perineal numbness: urgent spinal imaging (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Diagnosis).
Renal failure, urosepsis, severe comorbidity or poor follow-up: admit (AUR review 2007, Section Hospitalize vs. home).
Urine output above 200 mL/hour over input after drainage: post-obstructive diuresis, admit with hourly fluid replacement (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Treatment).
Clot retention from visible haematuria: three-way catheter and admission (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Special considerations).
Recent urological surgery or suspected false passage: call urology before or instead of further attempts (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Treatment).
precipitants: Anticholinergic medicines and alpha-agonist cold remedies (AUR review 2007, Section Medications and AUR).
Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs): about double the risk in current users (AUR review 2007, Section NSAIDs and AUR).
Surgery and anaesthesia, especially intravenous fluid over 750 mL (AUR review 2007, Section Postoperative AUR).
Urinary tract infection (AUR review 2007, Section Urinary tract infection).
Stroke and alcohol (AUR review 2007, Section Cerebrovascular accident and alcohol).
Faecal impaction (AUR review 2007, Section Constipation and AUR).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Older man with prior lower urinary tract symptoms and enlarged prostate (AUR review 2007, Section Epidemiology).

differentials.condition: Spinal cord or cauda equina compression
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Neurological deficit, reduced anal tone or perineal sensation (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Sections Clinical features and Diagnosis).
Visible haematuria with clots (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Special considerations).
Uncommon; usually gynaecological obstruction or neurogenic; pelvic ultrasound and urogynaecology referral (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Special considerations).
New anticholinergic, antihistamine or alpha-agonist (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Special considerations).

ruleIn.normalValue: Post-void residual below about 50 to 100 mL (typical adult value)

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Large drained volume; over 1.3 L in some patients
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Catheter treats and diagnoses; retention over 1.3 L benefits from longer catheterisation before TWOC; under 1 L predicts TWOC success (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Disposition; AUR review 2007, Section Trial without catheter).
ruleIn.normalValue: Normal bladder capacity about 400 to 600 mL (typical adult value)

clinicalManagement.title: Assess and confirm
actions: Take a urinary, drug and neurological history; examine abdomen, genitals and rectum including anal tone (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Clinical features).
Confirm with bedside bladder ultrasound (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Diagnosis).

clinicalManagement.title: Decompress the bladder
actions: Pass a urethral catheter first; if a standard catheter fails, try a coudé-tip catheter (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Treatment).
Do not inflate the balloon until urine drains freely (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Treatment).
After several failed attempts and with no pelvic trauma or abnormal anatomy, place an ultrasound-guided suprapubic catheter (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Treatment).
Recent urological surgery or suspected false passage: involve urology (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Treatment).
Re-examine the abdomen after drainage to exclude another cause of distension (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Clinical features).

clinicalManagement.title: Watch for post-obstructive diuresis
actions: Measure urine output; output over 200 mL/hour above input means admission with hourly volume replacement (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Treatment).
Send urinalysis, culture, creatinine and electrolytes (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Diagnosis).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat precipitants
actions: Stop anticholinergic, antihistamine and alpha-agonist medicines where possible and review NSAIDs use (AUR review 2007, Sections Medications and NSAIDs).
Treat urinary infection and faecal impaction (AUR review 2007, Sections Urinary tract infection and Constipation).

clinicalManagement.title: Start an alpha blocker and plan TWOC
actions: Men with BPH-related AUR: start alfuzosin before TWOC (see Medicines) (AUR review 2007, Section Role of alpha blockers).
Plan TWOC after 1 to 3 days; longer catheterisation raises haematuria, sepsis and leakage (AUR review 2007, Section Trial without catheter).

clinicalManagement.title: Disposition
actions: About 90% go home with a catheter and urology follow-up (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Disposition).

Admit for renal failure, urosepsis, severe comorbidity, clot retention or poor access to follow-up (AUR review 2007, Section Hospitalize vs. home; SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Special considerations).
TWOC in 3 to 7 days, later if retention volume was over 1.3 L (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Disposition).

regimens.indication: Improve chance of successful TWOC in BPH-related AUR
regimens.dose: 10 mg once daily with food, the same meal each day; do not chew or crush (Alfuzosin label, Section 2). In the ALFAUR trial alfuzosin 10 mg once daily raised TWOC success from 48% to 62% (AUR review 2007, Section Role of alpha blockers).
regimens.duration: From catheterisation until at least the TWOC; continue for BPH if voiding resumes (AUR review 2007, Section Role of alpha blockers)
adjustments: Severe renal impairment: use with caution; exposure rises about 50% (Alfuzosin label, Sections 5 and 8.6).
Moderate or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B or C): contraindicated (Alfuzosin label, Section 4).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Postural hypotension and dizziness within hours of the first dose; counsel the patient (Alfuzosin label, Section 5; SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Treatment).
Voiding and residual volume at TWOC.
contraindications: Moderate or severe hepatic impairment (Alfuzosin label, Section 4).
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole, itraconazole and ritonavir (Alfuzosin label, Section 4).
Caution: QT prolongation, planned cataract surgery (floppy iris syndrome) and rare priapism (Alfuzosin label, Sections 5.6, 5.7 and 5.9).

medicationPlan.note: Alfuzosin is the alpha blocker with trial evidence for TWOC in the opened sources. diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Sudden inability to pass urine with pain and a distended bladder confirmed by bedside ultrasound or catheter drainage (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Sections Definition and Diagnosis).
Precipitated if after surgery, stroke, infection or drugs; spontaneous AUR has higher recurrence and surgery rates (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Special considerations).
Urine output more than 200 mL/hour above input during at least 4 hours of monitoring (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Treatment).

teaching.scope: Adults with acute urinary retention (AUR) in the emergency department (ED) or primary care: recognition, bedside bladder ultrasound, urethral or suprapubic catheterisation, search for precipitants, post-obstructive diuresis, alpha blocker before a trial without catheter (TWOC), admission criteria and urology follow-up. Uses an ED clinical summary from South Eastern Sydney Local Health District (SESLHD), a peer-reviewed review of AUR in benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), and the alfuzosin label. Children and retention after recent urological surgery are excluded except for when to call urology.
learningObjectives: Confirm AUR with bladder ultrasound and decompress safely.
Start an alpha blocker before TWOC and know who to admit.
pitfalls: Repeated forceful catheter attempts causing a false passage.
Discharging a patient with post-obstructive diuresis.
Restarting anticholinergic drugs after the TWOC.
keyPoints: Check anal tone and perineal sensation in every patient.
Never inflate the balloon before urine flows.
Alfuzosin nearly doubles the chance of a successful TWOC.

patientEducation: The catheter drains urine until the prostate settles; a trial without it is planned in a few days.
Return for fever, vomiting, abdominal pain, catheter blockage or penile pain (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Disposition).
Stand up slowly after starting alfuzosin.
lifestyleAndDiet: Avoid cold remedies containing decongestants and anticholinergic sleep aids.
Avoid constipation and large amounts of alcohol.
mdtReferrals: Emergency physician; urologist; nursing staff for catheter care; general practitioner; urogynaecologist for women (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Special considerations).
dischargeCriteria: Catheter draining, no post-obstructive diuresis over 4 hours, renal function acceptable, no sepsis, alarm features explained, alfuzosin started, TWOC booked in 3 to 7 days (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Sections Treatment and Disposition).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Urology TWOC in 3 to 7 days (later if over 1.3 L drained); if TWOC fails, urology review for re-catheterisation and planned surgery (SESLHD ED AUR summary, Section Disposition; AUR review 2007, Section Trial without catheter).
